question: Mechanics of epoll's edge-triggered mode (EPOLLET) in Linux: how and when readiness is reported, the rules a program using it must follow, and the exact flags, calls and values involved.

facts.summary: In the page's pipe example (2 kB written, 1 kB read), an EPOLLET registration makes the second epoll_wait(2) likely to hang although unread data is still buffered, because the one event from the write was already consumed.
facts.quote: If the rfd file descriptor has been added to the epoll interface using the EPOLLET (edge-triggered) flag, the call to epoll_wait(2) done in step 5 will probably hang despite the available data still present in the file input buffer … Since the read operation done in 4 does not consume the whole buffer data, the call to epoll_wait(2) done in step 5 might block indefinitely.

facts.summary: Edge-triggered mode reports an event only when a change happens on the descriptor, one event per chunk of data received.
facts.quote: edge-triggered mode delivers events only when changes occur on the monitored file descriptor, that is, an event will be generated upon each receipt of a chunk of data.

facts.summary: A program using EPOLLET should use nonblocking descriptors and wait for a new event only after read(2) or write(2) has returned EAGAIN.
facts.quote: An application that employs the EPOLLET flag should use nonblocking file descriptors to avoid having a blocking read or write starve a task that is handling multiple file descriptors. The suggested way to use epoll as an edge-triggered (EPOLLET) interface is as follows: (1) with nonblocking file descriptors; and (2) by waiting for an event only after read(2) or write(2) return EAGAIN.

facts.summary: Level-triggered is the default when EPOLLET is not given, and then epoll has the same semantics as poll(2).
facts.quote: when used as a level-triggered interface (the default, when EPOLLET is not specified), epoll is simply a faster poll(2), and can be used wherever the latter is used since it shares the same semantics.

facts.summary: Even in edge-triggered mode several chunks can yield several events; EPOLLONESHOT disables the descriptor after one event, and the caller must rearm it with EPOLL_CTL_MOD.
facts.quote: Since even with edge-triggered epoll, multiple events can be generated upon receipt of multiple chunks of data, the caller has the option to specify the EPOLLONESHOT flag, to tell epoll to disable the associated file descriptor after the receipt of an event with epoll_wait(2). When the EPOLLONESHOT flag is specified, it is the caller's responsibility to rearm the file descriptor using epoll_ctl(2) with EPOLL_CTL_MOD.

facts.summary: When several threads or processes block in epoll_wait(2) on one epoll descriptor and an EPOLLET descriptor becomes ready, only one of them is woken.
facts.quote: If multiple threads (or processes, if child processes have inherited the epoll file descriptor across fork(2)) are blocked in epoll_wait(2) waiting on the same epoll file descriptor and a file descriptor in the interest list that is marked for edge-triggered (EPOLLET) notification becomes ready, just one of the threads (or processes) is awoken from epoll_wait(2).

facts.summary: In the page's example the handler uses a ready descriptor until read(2) or write(2) returns EAGAIN, and a state-machine program records where it stopped so the next call resumes there.
facts.quote: The function do_use_fd() uses the new ready file descriptor until EAGAIN is returned by either read(2) or write(2). An event-driven state machine application should, after having received EAGAIN, record its current state so that at the next call to do_use_fd() it will continue to read(2) or write(2) from where it stopped before.

facts.summary: With edge-triggered use, a descriptor may be added once with EPOLLIN|EPOLLOUT, which avoids switching between the two with EPOLL_CTL_MOD.
facts.quote: When used as an edge-triggered interface, for performance reasons, it is possible to add the file descriptor inside the epoll interface (EPOLL_CTL_ADD) once by specifying (EPOLLIN|EPOLLOUT). This allows you to avoid continuously switching between EPOLLIN and EPOLLOUT calling epoll_ctl(2) with EPOLL_CTL_MOD.

facts.summary: Several events that occur between two epoll_wait(2) calls are combined into one report.
facts.quote: If more than one event occurs between epoll_wait(2) calls, are they combined or reported separately? They will be combined.

facts.summary: A modify (EPOLL_CTL_MOD) on a registered descriptor re-reads the I/O that is available.
facts.quote: Does an operation on a file descriptor affect the already collected but not yet reported events? You can do two operations on an existing file descriptor. Remove would be meaningless for this case. Modify will reread available I/O.

facts.summary: After an event, the program must treat the descriptor as ready until a nonblocking read or write returns EAGAIN; when it does the I/O is up to the program.
facts.quote: Receiving an event from epoll_wait(2) should suggest to you that such file descriptor is ready for the requested I/O operation. You must consider it ready until the next (nonblocking) read/write yields EAGAIN. When and how you will use the file descriptor is entirely up to you.

facts.summary: For packet or token files the only end-of-data signal is EAGAIN; for stream files a short read or write also shows the space is exhausted, but only if the descriptor is surely a stream.
facts.quote: For packet/token-oriented files (e.g., datagram socket, terminal in canonical mode), the only way to detect the end of the read/write I/O space is to continue to read/write until EAGAIN. … For stream-oriented files (e.g., pipe, FIFO, stream socket), the condition that the read/write I/O space is exhausted can also be detected by checking the amount of data read from / written to the target file descriptor. … (Avoid this latter technique if you cannot guarantee that the monitored file descriptor always refers to a stream-oriented file.)

facts.summary: Draining one descriptor with a lot of I/O can starve the others; the page's remedy is an application-side ready list that round-robins among ready descriptors.
facts.quote: If there is a large amount of I/O space, it is possible that by trying to drain it the other files will not get processed causing starvation. (This problem is not specific to epoll.) The solution is to maintain a ready list and mark the file descriptor as ready in its associated data structure, thereby allowing the application to remember which files need to be processed but still round robin amongst all the ready files.

facts.summary: The events mask ORs event types, which epoll_wait(2) returns, with input flags, which change behaviour and are never returned.
facts.quote: The events member of the epoll_event structure is a bit mask composed by ORing together zero or more event types, returned by epoll_wait(2), and input flags, which affect its behavior, but aren't returned.

facts.summary: EPOLLET is an input flag that requests edge-triggered notification; without it epoll is level-triggered.
facts.quote: EPOLLET Requests edge-triggered notification for the associated file descriptor. The default behavior for epoll is level- triggered.

facts.summary: EPOLLRDHUP (since Linux 2.6.17) reports that a stream socket peer closed or shut down writing, and the page calls it especially useful for detecting peer shutdown under edge-triggered monitoring.
facts.quote: EPOLLRDHUP (since Linux 2.6.17) Stream socket peer closed connection, or shut down writing half of connection. (This flag is especially useful for writing simple code to detect peer shutdown when using edge-triggered monitoring.)

facts.summary: EPOLLERR is always reported by epoll_wait(2), so it need not be set in events.
facts.quote: EPOLLERR Error condition happened on the associated file descriptor. … epoll_wait(2) will always report for this event; it is not necessary to set it in events when calling epoll_ctl().

facts.summary: EPOLLHUP is always waited for; on a pipe or stream socket it only means the peer closed its end, and reads return 0 only after all buffered data is consumed.
facts.quote: EPOLLHUP Hang up happened on the associated file descriptor. epoll_wait(2) will always wait for this event; it is not necessary to set it in events when calling epoll_ctl(). Note that when reading from a channel such as a pipe or a stream socket, this event merely indicates that the peer closed its end of the channel. Subsequent reads from the channel will return 0 (end of file) only after all outstanding data in the channel has been consumed.

facts.summary: EPOLLONESHOT (since Linux 2.6.2) disables the descriptor in the interest list after one reported event; the user must rearm it with EPOLL_CTL_MOD and a new event mask.
facts.quote: EPOLLONESHOT (since Linux 2.6.2) Requests one-shot notification for the associated file descriptor. This means that after an event notified for the file descriptor by epoll_wait(2), the file descriptor is disabled in the interest list and no other events will be reported by the epoll interface. The user must call epoll_ctl() with EPOLL_CTL_MOD to rearm the file descriptor with a new event mask.

facts.summary: EPOLLWAKEUP (since Linux 3.5) keeps the system from suspending while an event is pending or processed, only when EPOLLONESHOT and EPOLLET are clear and the process has CAP_BLOCK_SUSPEND.
facts.quote: EPOLLWAKEUP (since Linux 3.5) If EPOLLONESHOT and EPOLLET are clear and the process has the CAP_BLOCK_SUSPEND capability, ensure that the system does not enter "suspend" or "hibernate" while this event is pending or being processed.

facts.summary: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE exists since Linux 4.5 and sets an exclusive wakeup mode for the epoll descriptor attached to the target.
facts.quote: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE (since Linux 4.5) Sets an exclusive wakeup mode for the epoll file descriptor that is being attached to the target file descriptor, fd.

facts.summary: With EPOLLEXCLUSIVE only EPOLLIN, EPOLLOUT, EPOLLWAKEUP and EPOLLET (plus EPOLLHUP and EPOLLERR) may be given; any other value fails with EINVAL.
facts.quote: The following values may be specified in conjunction with EPOLLEXCLUSIVE: EPOLLIN, EPOLLOUT, EPOLLWAKEUP, and EPOLLET. EPOLLHUP and EPOLLERR can also be specified, but this is not required … Attempts to specify other values in events yield the error EINVAL.

facts.summary: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE is allowed only with EPOLL_CTL_ADD; using it with EPOLL_CTL_MOD, or a later MOD on a pair that has it, fails with EINVAL.
facts.quote: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE may be used only in an EPOLL_CTL_ADD operation; attempts to employ it with EPOLL_CTL_MOD yield an error. If EPOLLEXCLUSIVE has been set using epoll_ctl(), then a subsequent EPOLL_CTL_MOD on the same epfd, fd pair yields an error. … The error in all of these cases is EINVAL.

facts.summary: EPOLL_CTL_MOD replaces the settings of a registered descriptor with those in event.
facts.quote: EPOLL_CTL_MOD Change the settings associated with fd in the interest list to the new settings specified in event.

facts.summary: EPOLL_CTL_ADD of a descriptor already registered on the instance fails with EEXIST.
facts.quote: EEXIST op was EPOLL_CTL_ADD, and the supplied file descriptor fd is already registered with this epoll instance.

facts.summary: EPOLL_CTL_MOD or EPOLL_CTL_DEL of a descriptor not registered on the instance fails with ENOENT.
facts.quote: ENOENT op was EPOLL_CTL_MOD or EPOLL_CTL_DEL, and fd is not registered with this epoll instance.

facts.summary: A target that does not support epoll, such as a regular file or a directory, makes epoll_ctl() fail with EPERM.
facts.quote: EPERM The target file fd does not support epoll. This error can occur if fd refers to, for example, a regular file or a directory.

facts.summary: In Linux v6.12, after an event is copied to user space, an item without EPOLLONESHOT and without EPOLLET is put back on the ready list so the next epoll_wait() checks it again; an EPOLLET item is not put back.
facts.quote: else if (!(epi->event.events & EPOLLET)) { … If this file has been added with Level Trigger mode, we need to insert back inside the ready list, so that the next call to epoll_wait() will check again the events availability. … list_add_tail(&epi->rdllink, &ep->rdllist);

facts.summary: After delivering an event for an EPOLLONESHOT item, the kernel clears every bit of its event mask except the private flag bits.
facts.quote: if (epi->event.events & EPOLLONESHOT) epi->event.events &= EP_PRIVATE_BITS;

facts.summary: The private flag bits are EPOLLWAKEUP, EPOLLONESHOT, EPOLLET and EPOLLEXCLUSIVE.
facts.quote: #define EP_PRIVATE_BITS (EPOLLWAKEUP | EPOLLONESHOT | EPOLLET | EPOLLEXCLUSIVE)

facts.summary: When events are collected, each ready-list item is unlinked and its file polled again under ep->mtx; an item whose poll now returns no requested event is skipped, not reported.
facts.quote: list_del_init(&epi->rdllink); … If the event mask intersect the caller-requested one, deliver the event to userspace. … revents = ep_item_poll(epi, &pt, 1); if (!revents) continue;

facts.summary: At the end of a collection pass, items left over are spliced back onto the ready list, and if it is not empty a waiter on the epoll instance is woken.
facts.quote: Quickly re-inject items left on "txlist". … list_splice(txlist, &ep->rdllist); … if (!list_empty(&ep->rdllist)) { if (waitqueue_active(&ep->wq)) wake_up(&ep->wq);

facts.summary: The wakeup callback ignores an item whose mask holds no poll event bits, which is how a fired EPOLLONESHOT item stays disabled until the next EPOLL_CTL_MOD.
facts.quote: If the event mask does not contain any poll(2) event, we consider the descriptor to be disabled. This condition is likely the effect of the EPOLLONESHOT bit that disables the descriptor when an event is received, until the next EPOLL_CTL_MOD will be issued. … if (!(epi->event.events & ~EP_PRIVATE_BITS)) goto out_unlock;

facts.summary: The source gives the reason EPOLLEXCLUSIVE is refused for EPOLL_CTL_MOD: epoll joins the target's wakeup queue only at EPOLL_CTL_ADD.
facts.quote: epoll adds to the wakeup queue at EPOLL_CTL_ADD time only, so EPOLLEXCLUSIVE is not allowed for a EPOLL_CTL_MOD operation.

facts.quote: The maximum number of event must be greater than zero … if (maxevents <= 0 || maxevents > EP_MAX_EVENTS) return -EINVAL;

facts.quote: #define EPOLL_CTL_ADD 1 … #define EPOLL_CTL_DEL 2 … #define EPOLL_CTL_MOD 3

facts.summary: EPOLLET is bit 31 of the event mask (1U << 31) and sets edge-triggered behaviour for the target descriptor.
facts.quote: Set the Edge Triggered behaviour for the target file descriptor … #define EPOLLET ((__force __poll_t)(1U << 31))

facts.quote: Set the One Shot behaviour for the target file descriptor … #define EPOLLONESHOT ((__force __poll_t)(1U << 30))

facts.quote: Set exclusive wakeup mode for the target file descriptor … #define EPOLLEXCLUSIVE ((__force __poll_t)(1U << 28))

facts.summary: EPOLLWAKEUP is bit 29 (1U << 29), needs CAP_BLOCK_SUSPEND, and its hold on suspend until the next epoll_wait is stated for the case where neither EPOLLET nor EPOLLONESHOT is set.
facts.quote: Assuming neither EPOLLET nor EPOLLONESHOT is set, system suspends will not be re-allowed until epoll_wait is called again after consuming the wakeup event(s). … Requires CAP_BLOCK_SUSPEND … #define EPOLLWAKEUP ((__force __poll_t)(1U << 29))

facts.summary: The event bits are EPOLLIN = 0x001, EPOLLOUT = 0x004, EPOLLERR = 0x008 and EPOLLHUP = 0x010.
facts.quote: #define EPOLLIN (__force __poll_t)0x00000001 … #define EPOLLOUT (__force __poll_t)0x00000004 … #define EPOLLERR (__force __poll_t)0x00000008 … #define EPOLLHUP (__force __poll_t)0x00000010

facts.summary: struct epoll_event holds a __poll_t events mask and a __u64 data field, and is packed on x86-64 so the 64-bit layout matches the 32-bit one.
facts.quote: #ifdef __x86_64__ … #define EPOLL_PACKED __attribute__((packed)) … struct epoll_event { __poll_t events; __u64 data; } EPOLL_PACKED;

conflicts.topic: is the one-waiter wakeup specific to EPOLLET descriptors?
conflicts.note: epoll(7) states the one-thread wakeup for an EPOLLET descriptor; the v6.12 source queues every epoll_wait waiter as exclusive with no EPOLLET test, and ep_done_scan wakes another waiter when the ready list is not empty

conflicts.topic: one event per chunk of data, or one per epoll_wait call?
conflicts.note: epoll(7) says edge-triggered mode generates an event on each chunk received; its own FAQ says events between epoll_wait calls are combined, and the source links an item to the ready list only when it is not already linked
